title: "Case study: ants along Mt Wilhelm and in rainforest canopies"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev.args = list(bg = "white"),
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 150, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4
)
```

Two Papua New Guinea ant datasets show tidydiversity on incidence-type and
nest-count data.

**Sources and licences.** `png_ants`: Moses et al. (2023), data deposited
on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946) and included with the lead
author's permission. `png_tree_ants`: Plowman et al. (2020), data on Dryad
(doi:10.5061/dryad.2fqz612k6) under CC0 1.0. See `?png_ants`,
`?png_tree_ants` and `data-raw/` for how each was built.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(2026)
```

## Ground ants at baits along Mt Wilhelm

Baits were set at eight elevations from 200 to 3700 m in the dry and the
wet season. Worker counts at a bait reflect recruitment, so each species
at a bait counts as one occurrence (the default when the data have no
`abundance` column).

```{r baits}
png_ants
div_coverage(png_ants, .by = season)
```

Coverage differs between seasons and sites, so compare richness at equal
coverage:

```{r baits-std, fig.alt = "Coverage-standardised ant richness along Mt Wilhelm by season"}
std <- div_standardise(png_ants, q = 0, .by = season, nboot = 100) |>
  add_site_data(distinct(png_ants, site, elevation))
ggplot(std, aes(elevation, diversity, colour = season)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    position = position_dodge(width = 80)
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_tidydiversity() +
  labs(x = "Elevation (m)", y = "Richness at equal coverage", colour = NULL) +
  theme_tidydiversity()
```

Both seasons cover the same five elevations, 200 to 2200 m (a single
dry-season record at 2700 m is left out of `png_ants` to keep the seasons
comparable). Richness peaks at low to mid
elevation and falls sharply above 1700 m.

## Tree-nesting ants in three forest plots

`png_tree_ants` lists every ant nest in 1254 trees in plots at Wanang
(200 m), Numba (900 m) and Yawan (1800 m). Using the number of nests as
the abundance and pooling trees within each plot:

```{r trees}
est <- div_estimate(png_tree_ants, abundance = nests, nboot = 100)
est
```

```{r trees-plot, fig.alt = "Asymptotic Hill numbers of tree-nesting ants in three plots"}
autoplot(est)
```

Diversity of every order peaks at mid elevation (Numba), as Plowman et al.
(2020) reported. Estimated richness at Yawan has a wide interval because
many species there were found only once.

Treating each tree as a site, almost all dissimilarity between trees is
turnover rather than nestedness:

```{r trees-beta}
beta_multi(png_tree_ants, site = tree, .by = site)
```
